name: National Valley Girl lexical fad
description: Ephemeral lexical formulas circulated through the 1982 Valley Girl recording, press coverage, merchandising, and associated adolescent imitation.
cause_of_death: Rapid internal replacement and immediate caricature are documented in 1982. The national merchandising-wave fade is estimated; persistent discourse features are excluded.

sources.title: Living: How Toe-dully Max Is Their Valley, page 1
sources.note: Contemporaneous Michael Demarest article inspected. Documents national merchandising, the Zappa single, and journalistic imitation of the register.

sources.title: Living: How Toe-dully Max Is Their Valley, page 2
sources.note: Contemporaneous article inspected. Calls the vocabulary ephemeral and explicitly identifies bitchen and tubular as already displaced Valley staples.

sources.title: Valley girl: source text
sources.note: Source text inspected. Identifies the 1982 single as popularizing grody to the max and gag me with a spoon; notes continuing mainstream features, which are excluded here.

sources.title: Ship Arriving Too Late to Save a Drowning Witch
sources.note: Official release page inspected. Confirms the album release date, Valley Girl track, and Moon Zappa vocal credit; does not supply term-frequency measurements.

entries.gloss: An emphatic affirmative in phonetic Valley spelling.

examples.text: Fer shurr, I can collect the printouts before the meeting.

entries.rationale: The inspected 1982 TIME account attests 'fer shurr' in the national Valley Girl moment. TIME explicitly describes rapidly changing, ephemeral vocabulary and the register's national merchandising in September 1982. Parameters describe this particular appropriation, not the invention of older surf language; onset and fade are estimated without annual frequency measurements.
